sections.html:
The recorder works from Room 203 of the Celina courthouse, 101 N. Main Street, Celina, Ohio 45822. Call (419) 586-4232 to reach staff. Doors open at half past eight each weekday. Mondays run later, to five, while Tuesday through Friday end at four. The office closes on federal holidays.

Anything that deals with land can be recorded there and read by the public. Recording is paid in cash or by check payable to the Mercer County Recorder. Cards are not accepted for recording. Copy requests are the exception, because the office has an online payment link for card or eCheck.

Ohio Senate Bill 94 took effect October 24, 2024. It lets a recorder add a preservation surcharge of up to $5.00 per document, and Mercer County began charging it January 1, 2025. The base is $39.00 through page two and $8.00 for each page after that.

Mercer County recording fee by page count
PagesFee

4$55.00
5$63.00
6$71.00
7$79.00
8$87.00

References add $4.00 each, and the formatting rules below still apply. Papers that carry their own fee under the Revised Code, among them federal tax liens, plats, township zoning and UCC filings, skip the new $5.00 charge.

Ohio's standardization law, ORC 317.114, covers documents prepared after June 30, 2009. A paper that misses the mark draws a $20.00 charge. The recorder's standard looks like this:

  • Print in a font of at least ten points.
  • Use paper no smaller than letter size and no longer than 14 inches.
  • Use black or blue ink with no highlighter.
  • Keep a one-inch border at the sides and bottom.
  • Leave three inches clear at the head of the first page, where the recorder, auditor and engineer stamp, and an inch and a half at the top of later pages.

The rules exempt court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD214 forms, state or federal documents and anything signed before the law took effect. The office also wants an original rather than a photocopy, a legal description, the preparer's name, a notary and English text. A deed that conveys land has to clear the Tax Map office and the auditor before it gets to the recorder.

A quick check before you leave home saves a second trip. Confirm the original is signed and notarized, the legal description matches the Tax Map approval, and the check is written to the right office for the right amount. A cash sale needs no lender paperwork, so the deed packet is usually the whole filing.

sections.h2: Can a deed go in by mail or e-recording?
sections.html:
Both routes are open. Since November 1, 2024 the auditor, tax map and recorder offices have accepted mail-in conveyances together, under firm conditions. The Tax Map office must approve the legal description first, and the packet needs the email showing it did.

  • Complete the auditor's forms.
  • Send separate checks to the auditor, the recorder and the treasurer. A combined check gets the packet rejected.
  • Add any recording instructions and a return envelope with postage.

Expect a one-day turnaround by mail and an immediate one at the counter. Electronic filing has been taking documents since 2010, and from November 5, 2025 conveyances can be sent through all three vendors (Simplifile, CSC and ePN). Title companies and lenders usually handle that for you.

sections.h2: Copies of recorded deeds and sheriff's sales
sections.html:
Prints made by the office cost $2.00 a page. Deeds recorded since 1946 can be viewed and printed free from the recorder's records search website. For a mailed copy, send the owner name or property address and the exact fee, plus a stamped envelope addressed to yourself, to the Room 203 address, or email the office. Staff cannot do title searches.

The recorder is the last office to see paperwork from a sheriff's sale. After a foreclosure ends, the Mercer County Sheriff's Office sends the sheriff's deed to the recorder. The sheriff keeps a searchable list of properties going up for sale, and you can read the foreclosure case itself on the Clerk of Courts website once you have the case number.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed: what to ask the treasurer
sections.html:
The treasurer's office is Room 201 in the courthouse, reachable at (419) 586-2259. Ohio bills real estate tax one year behind. Who owes what at a sale therefore comes down to the closing agreement, and tax that falls due after the purchase date belongs to the buyer.

Bills are mailed in January and June, usually with payment due on the 20th of February and July. Pay within ten days of the deadline and the penalty is 5 percent. Pay later and it is 10 percent. A remission application goes before the Board of Revision (treasurer, auditor and a commissioner). Monthly ACH or coupon plans are available too.

A delinquency notice goes out in late September. Parcels still unpaid in early November with no installment plan are advertised. Request a payoff figure well ahead of closing, so any penalty is paid from your proceeds and not left for the buyer to find.

The auditor's 2026 triennial update reviews arm's-length sale prices from 2023, 2024 and 2025. It does not repeat the full exterior inspection of each parcel done for the 2023 reappraisal. New values will appear on the 2027 tax bills.

The Inflation Cap Credit from House Bill 186 reached second-half 2025 bills payable in 2026. Every parcel gets its own figure, and a few get none. Any overpayment rolls into the first-half 2026 bill. The auditor's site includes a conveyance fee calculator, which is the place to get the county's rate for a sale.

Mercer County lies along Ohio's border with Indiana. Celina holds the courthouse and is the county's only city, and Grand Lake St. Marys is the largest inland lake in Ohio. The county had 42,737 people in July 2025, a small gain over 2020, and the housing numbers describe a steady owner market.

  • Close to four in five households (79.6 percent) own their homes, out of 16,408 households.
  • The middle owner-occupied house is valued at $210,600.
  • Those paying a mortgage spend $1,340 a month on owner costs, and those without spend $553.
  • Renters pay $804 in median gross rent.
  • Household income is $76,782 at the median.
  • Builders pulled 83 permits in 2025 for a stock of 18,384 housing units.

faqs.q: When can you reach the Mercer County Recorder?
faqs.a: It opens at 8:30 a.m. on weekdays, closes at five on Mondays and at four Tuesday through Friday, and shuts on federal holidays. The office is in Room 203 of the courthouse at 101 N. Main Street in Celina.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a short Mercer County deed?
faqs.a: A deed of one or two pages costs $39.00. Each further page adds $8.00, and a $4.00 reference fee or a $20.00 non-standard charge may apply.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees with a card in Mercer County?
faqs.a: No. Recording is paid by check or cash, with checks payable to the Mercer County Recorder. Copy requests can be paid by card or eCheck online.

faqs.q: What does a veteran pay to record a DD214 in Mercer County?
faqs.a: Nothing. The office records a DD214 and issues copies free. Copies go only to authorized people with identification, such as the veteran or an estate executor.

faqs.q: Since when can conveyance deeds be e-recorded in Mercer County?
faqs.a: Conveyance documents have gone through each of the office's three e-recording vendors since November 5, 2025. Other e-recordings began in 2010.
